{{Top}}
{{Otheruses|Tarkin}}
[[File:Tarkin_UM.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] epitomized the Tarkin Doctrine.]]
{{Quote|Fear will keep the local systems in line. Fear of this battle station.|Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
The '''Tarkin Doctrine''', also known as the '''Doctrine of Terror''', '''Rule of Fear''',<ref name="RB">{{JournalCite|9|Repulsortank Battlefield}}</ref> '''Doctrine of Fear''',<ref name="GoF_PP">''[[Galaxy of Fear: Planet Plague]]''</ref> and officially known as '''Imperial Communiqué #001044.92v''', was a message originally sent directly to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] from then [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]. The transmission detailed Tarkin's concept of maintaining order and increasing security within the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] by means of state terrorism. It became one of the most important documents regarding Imperial policy.

==Overview==
{{Quote|The more you tighten your grip, Tarkin, the more star systems will slip through your fingers.|Princess Leia|audio=LeiaSlipThroughYourFingers.flac|<ref name="Episode 4" />}}
[[File:TarkinDoctrine_swptp.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Tarkin, discussing his doctrine]]
The Tarkin Doctrine was an evolutionary concept. It had its roots in [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], when [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar]] presented his plans for the [[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]] to then-[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] Tarkin. Tarkin was fascinated by the concept: as an officer in the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]], he had seen the chaos caused by the absence of government in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. His own experience with the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] was also a factor in this, as it split the galaxy into thousands of sectors with a senator each claiming to represent trillions of citizens, which led to chaos.<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> To create a [[Navy/Legends|navy]] large enough to police [[The galaxy/Legends|the entire galaxy]] would be ruinously expensive, and could still be overcome by an opponent making use of hit-and-run strikes and a [[stateless strategy]]. Tarkin saw Sienar's design, improved with the addition of a weapon powerful enough to seriously damage a planet, as the solution to this strategic conundrum: no world, he believed, would dare harbor pirates or defy central authority if the punishment was the destruction of their planet.<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> He also had experience with how he was trying to pursue pirates within his sector, only for them to go deep into another sector, where they would exploit jurisdiction laws where Tarkin was unable to continue his pursuit without possibly entering conflict with another moff.<ref name="DSTC">''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''</ref>

Tarkin plagiarized Sienar's concept and presented it to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who ordered the beginning of research that would eventually lead to the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> Another influence on the development of the Tarkin Doctrine was the creation of the [[Sector Army/Legends|sector armies]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the re-installation of the office of the [[Governor-General/Legends|Governor-Generals]], which overrode existing [[Sector/Legends|sector]] borders<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

Tarkin presented his complete concept to Emperor Palpatine in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]]. The Doctrine called for three primary principles: Territorial Consolidation; Rapid Communication; and, most infamously, the Rule of Fear.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

Under Territorial Consolidation,<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> to deal with cross-sector criminal and rebellious activity and the problem of jurisdictional conflicts, the Tarkin Doctrine called for the retooling of the sector armies' areas of operations to create [[Oversector/Legends|Oversectors]], proposing they be tailored to control unstable galactic hot spots and be assigned greater forces than usual in an attempt to root out [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|rebellious]] activity before it could take hold. Each Oversector, capable of crossing traditional sector boundaries, would be controlled by a single official who answered directly to Palpatine.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Under Rapid Communication, the Tarkin Doctrine also called for the cannibalization of the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] and its restriction to the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]],<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> as well as the overall [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]],<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> in order to deny communication to insurgents and to more effectively coordinate [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Groups]].<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> According to Tarkin, this was because the HoloNet, allowing face-to-face communication across thousands of [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]], was far too valuable to let the public have free access. Under this method, each sector [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] would receive its own transceiver and remain in direct contact with [[Oversector/Legends|Oversector]] command, while Oversector command would maintain a direct link with Imperial High Command on Coruscant. Another reason for this implementation was to ensure that far-flung Imperial sectors could no longer run wild from a lack of discipline by making sure central authority watched their every move.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

[[File:Grand_Moff_Tarkin_2015_World_Championship_Prize.png|thumb|right|200px|Grand Moff Tarkin on the bridge of an Imperial Star Destroyer]]
Finally, the cornerstone of the Doctrine was the concept of "rule through fear of force, rather than through force itself," also most infamously known as the Rule of Fear. Displays of power, most vitally through the use of terror-inspiring [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]], would, Tarkin suggested, stifle dissent and rebellion. The presentation of a seemingly invincible weapon of ultimate power would play upon the fearfulness and awe of the citizenry to render all thought of assault against the Empire forgotten.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" /> It was therefore Tarkin's recommendation that the Empire invest strongly and continually in the innovation of ever more-powerful weapons of war.<ref name="Star Wars: Force Commander">''[[Star Wars: Force Commander]]''</ref> The inspiration behind the creation of the rule of fear, and more specifically the research into superweapons development, was due to increased Rebel activity, and more specifically that the Rebels were now capable of not only fighting various Imperial troops, but also engaging in [[Space warfare/Legends|conventional naval warfare]] and destroying armored vehicles during a planetary invasion, meaning the Imperial military's superiority in equipment, training, and numbers would not be enough.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

Emperor Palpatine was very impressed with the ideas, so much that all the suggestions were implemented with Tarkin promoted to the new rank of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] (making him the first Grand Moff). Tarkin's own sector army's theater, the [[Greater Seswenna/Legends|Greater Seswenna]], was dramatically expanded to become [[Oversector Outer]], which encompassed most of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. In addition, he was given command of four Sector Groups to crush insurgent activity, and was placed in command of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star project]], which fulfilled his philosophy of creating a weapon so powerful no planet would dare countenance resistance. According to the Tarkin Doctrine, once the Death Star was active, no one would dare act against the Empire. Terror at the prospect of planetary annihilation would ensure compliance and order.<ref name="Death Star novel">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref> The Tarkin Doctrine was also later included in the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', which was ironically published to the Imperial Military commanders shortly before a cornerstone of the Tarkin Doctrine, the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|First Death Star]], along with Tarkin himself, was [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destroyed]] at [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

The Empire was ultimately unsuccessful in instilling the fear necessary to keep the galaxy in line. Palpatine increasingly changed Tarkin's original words to his own meaning, "Rule through fear instead of through idealistic government agencies." Consequently, with the Death Star fully operational in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|dissolved the Imperial Senate]] with the battle station to be the principal source of Imperial control in the Outer Rim.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" /> However, the Death Star produced the opposite of its intended result&mdash;instead of cowering under the threat of such a weapon, the people viewed its victims (particularly the unarmed planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]) as martyrs and rallied to the Rebellion's cause, especially after the Death Star's destruction at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Further Imperial attempts to enact the doctrine with projects like the [[Tarkin (superweapon)|''Tarkin'']], a stripped-down [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] named in honor of the martyred Grand Moff, and the even larger [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star]], met with destruction in concerted Rebel strikes. The Empire was thus left in the same strategic conundrum the Tarkin Doctrine had been formulated to correct, and throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] the Imperial Navy was never able to bring enough ships to bear to properly police the Outer Rim.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

Aside from the flaws relating to the Rule of Fear, there were also some flaws encountered in the implementation of the other two principles. According to the ace Rebel pilot [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], a flaw in the first principle was a Grand Moff's jurisdiction crossing sector borders; accordingly, the Rebels changed their strategy by staging raids at the border of an oversector and then drawing two Grand Moffs into a turf war (which was ironically the reason he formed the first rule in the first place<ref name="DSTC" />). Likewise, the smuggler-turned-Rebel General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] mentioned that a week after the implementation of the Tarkin Doctrine, bootleg transceivers could be bought from any hustler on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], thus defeating the intended purpose of the second principle.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />

==Behind the scenes==
The full text of Imperial Communiqu&eacute; #001044.92v first appeared in the ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''. It appears again in the ''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]'', with different wording from the ''Imperial Sourcebook'' version while retaining much of the same meaning. The ''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]'' shows yet another, significantly shorter, version of this communiqu&eacute;.
